I will request a standard chest X-ray (PA and lateral).

[TEST] Chest X-ray (posteroanterior and lateral).

[THOUGHT] In a long-term smoker with progressive exertional dyspnea, occasional dry cough, and a normal chest X-ray, the next high-yield step is pulmonary function testing to distinguish obstructive disease (COPD/asthma), loss of diffusion capacity (emphysema or pulmonary vascular disease), or a restrictive pattern (interstitial lung disease). A full PFT with pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry plus DLCO will provide critical diagnostic direction.

[TEST] Pulmonary function tests: spirometry pre- and post-bronchodilator with lung volumes and diffusion capacity (DLCO).

4. Diffusion_Capacity: Decreased.

[THOUGHT] The patient is a long-term heavy smoker with progressive exertional dyspnea and occasional dry cough. PFTs show an obstructive pattern (FEV1/FVC 62%, FEV1 60% predicted), hyperinflation (TLC 125%), and a reduced DLCO. This combination is most consistent with emphysema-predominant COPD rather than asthma or interstitial or cardiac causes.

[DIAGNOSIS] Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (emphysema-predominant).
